definition: A small vision-language checkpoint, used in both sources as the scale at which a multimodal method is developed before being confirmed at 7B. In one it is the primary backbone for a step-wise visual grounding framework and carries most of the ablations — the layer sweep, the grounding-strategy comparison, and the explicit-versus-implicit contrast. In the other it appears in work on RLVR eroding general capability. Neither characterizes the model itself.

evidence.note: Reformulates chart question answering as a chain in which every reasoning step carries a predicted image region, trains that pairing through a curriculum graded by nesting depth, and finds explicit intermediate grounding worth 8.78 points over letting the model attend implicitly.
evidence.title: CURV: Enhancing Chart Understanding Through Curriculum Visual Grounded Reasoning

evidence.note: Splits a spatial-reasoning chain of thought into explicitly typed segments -- perception, including depth, and reasoning -- and gives each its own process reward and its own advantage term, so that the two do not compete for credit under a single outcome signal.
evidence.title: SCOUT: Unlocking Enhanced Spatial Reasoning via Structured Chain-of-Thought and Multi-Objective Process Reward

evidence.note: Confirms that prolonged RLVR makes models forget foundational skills, and counters it with experience replay whose objective weights adapt online to convergence and instability signals.
evidence.title: Beyond Reasoning Gains: Mitigating General-Capability Forgetting in Large Reasoning Models

name: Qwen2.5-VL-3B
